summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a 14-quarter high of Rs 1,179 crore (+12% YoY) and EBITDA rose 11% YoY to Rs 172 crore; FY27 guided to at least 20% EBITDA growth.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 as its strongest quarter in 14 quarters, with revenue of Rs 1,179 crore (+12% YoY, 10% volume-led), EBITDA of Rs 172 crore (+11% YoY, +26% QoQ) and PAT of Rs 86 crore (+17% YoY). Pass-through of crude-linked cost increases after the Middle East disruption supported pricing, and acetyls benefited from inventory bought before the price spike. Net debt to EBITDA fell to 0.99x and net working capital improved to 59 days. Management reiterated at least 20% full-year EBITDA growth for FY27 and expects sequential growth from Q1 FY27.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 5 per share (final Rs 2.5), cash outflow Rs 79.8 crore

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 516 crore (+6% YoY, +13% QoQ) and EBITDA Rs 139 crore at 27% margin, held for six quarters; pyridine volumes grew strongly and CDMO realisations rose. Management sees a sustainable margin of 23-25% after corporate overheads (about 25% before).

segments.name: Nutrition
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 230 crore (+21% YoY, +15% QoQ) and EBITDA Rs 32 crore (+42% QoQ) at 14% margin; FY26 revenue Rs 790 crore and EBITDA Rs 100 crore. Growth led by niacinamide volumes; Remidex Pharma acquisition completed for human nutrition premixes.

segments.name: Chemical Intermediates (acetyls)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 433 crore (+15% YoY, +10% QoQ) with EBITDA improvement from cost pass-through. Management expects favourable pricing as acetic acid prices rise, though acetic acid is now falling and inventory losses are possible.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA growth of at least 20% YoY, aspirational; management declined to guide quarterly growth rates.
Sequential revenue and EBITDA growth expected from Q1 FY27 onward.
Annual capex of Rs 400-500 crore in FY27; Gajraula MPP plant to finish in FY27 with production commencing in Q4 FY27.
Pinnacle target of 3x revenue and 4x EBITDA by FY30 retained on an organic basis, with pricing a key assumption.
Acetyls inventory impact expected to be absorbed in Q1 or early Q2 FY27.
capex_capacity: Capital WIP fell to about Rs 150 crore after the Bharuch CDMO plant was capitalised in March 2026 (commissioned in 14 months).
Gajraula MPP plant is the largest capex item and is under construction.
Pyridine and picoline capacity about 50,000 tonnes, run at 90%+ utilisation.
Human-grade niacin/niacinamide plant: PC-grade niacinamide at about 50% of estimated volumes; niacin ramp gradual, targeting 40-50% of peak volumes this year.
demand_pricing: Chemical demand resilient despite Middle East disruption; pricing firmed on crude-linked costs and pass-through.

CDMO growing 30-40% a year historically; a $300 million agro contract began shipping in March 2026, with the customer providing visibility only for Q1 FY27 volumes and a make-whole clause for any shortfall.

CDMO pipeline: 100+ opportunities worth about Rs 3,500 crore potential, 20+ confirmed molecules and 10+ advanced molecules with peak potential of Rs 1,100 crore; about 40% of pharma leads now from innovators.
Pyridine pricing at a low, while beta-picoline is at its highest in years; Chinese pyridine capacity runs at 30-40% utilisation.
Semiconductor chemicals: small commercial volumes so far, slow ramp-up expected; about a dozen projects in progress.

qa_highlights.question: How will acetyl spreads and inventory gains/losses play out in Q1 and beyond, given falling prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory bought during the price spike helped Q4 and should continue into Q1; any inventory loss is expected to be absorbed within Q1 or early Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA growth be quantified quarter by quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined quarterly guidance because single contract timing causes lumpiness; it reiterated at least 20% full-year EBITDA growth, with linear progression across quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 capex and how is CWIP falling?
qa_highlights.answer: CWIP fell after the Bharuch CDMO plant was capitalised; FY27 capex is Rs 400-500 crore per year, with the Gajraula MPP as the main project finishing in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company benefiting from the weaker rupee on the $300 million contract?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the benefit will not be linear: dollar imports roughly equal exports, so the company is naturally hedged, and some raw materials and equipment are dollar-linked.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the agro innovator contract volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Visibility is only for Q1 FY27; the customer has committed to make up any shortfall under the contract, and management expects at least last year's volume with upside.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Pyridine pricing muted and what is the sustainable Specialty margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Pyridine is at a low while beta-picoline is high; the two offset each other. Sustainable Specialty margin is 23-25% after overheads, with CDMO growth as a positive and trading cost pressure as a negative.

risks_watch: Acetyls inventory losses if acetic acid prices keep falling; Q2 FY27 is the key test.
Concentration risk in the $300 million agro CDMO contract: volume visibility beyond Q1 FY27 is still pending.
Pharma CDMO pipeline attrition: Phase II/III molecules may not reach commercial scale.
Management's FY30 target depends on pricing that management itself flags as a key assumption.
Slow ramp-up in semiconductor chemicals and agrochemical CDMO wins.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and FY27 growth, but cautious and somewhat hedged on pricing, agro volume visibility and the timing of new CDMO revenues. Management declined to give quarterly EBITDA or CDMO revenue numbers.
key_quotes: We had the highest quarterly revenue and EBITDA in Q4 FY '26 when compared with last 14 quarters with healthy double-digit growth in both top line and bottom line, reflecting our strong execution.
We still feel confident that by FY30, we should be able to take our EBITDA organically to the ranges that we announced in the Investor Day.
But we do have an understanding as well as commitment from them that just in case there is any shortfall in volumes, they will make us whole as per the contractual agreement.

adds.what: Gajraula MPP plant (largest capex item, under construction; production commencing Q4 FY27)
Bharuch CDMO plant (capitalised March 2026, commissioned in 14 months)

growth.why: Management aspires to at least 20% FY27 EBITDA growth (held) and sequential revenue and EBITDA growth from Q1 FY27, backed partly by Gajraula MPP plant (production Q4 FY27), a Rs 400-500 crore annual capex plan, pass-through pricing and a $300m agro CDMO contract with visibility only for Q1 FY27 volumes; no quantified revenue guide and quarterly growth not guided.
